rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without a legitimate excuse, one who can profess faith but withholds it is an unbeliever before God; under compelling coercion, profession is waived and inward faith suffices.
rows.anchor: Lâkin ikrâh-ı mülcî zarûret ve mazereti karşısında bunun vücûbu sâkıt olur. Ve o zaman yalnız îmân-ı kalbî kâfîdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some public religious practices, such as congregational prayer, can serve in place of a verbal profession of faith.
rows.anchor: Şu kadar ki cemaatle namaz kılmak gibi şe‘âirden olan bazı a‘mâl dahi ikrar makamına kāimdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In its legal sense, faith includes assent together with verbal profession and submission, since scriptural usage joins faith to bi or lam.
rows.anchor: Fi’l-vâki‘îmân-ı şer‘î dâima bâ veya lâm ile sılalandığından ikrâr u inkıyâd ile tasdik mânalarını mutazammındır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam addresses the whole person, inwardly and outwardly; absent an impediment, scripture and Sunna show that faith should not be kept private and unannounced.
rows.anchor: imanını yalnız kalbinde saklayan ve izhâr u i‘lan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good works are the intended fruit of faith, but the acts themselves are neither identical with faith nor a part of its essence; they are its branches and consequences.
rows.anchor: nefs-i amel, nefs-i îmânın aynı veya cüz’ü değildir. Fer‘i ve netâic-i matlûbesidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He compares faith to a fruit tree: inward assent is its underground root, profession its trunk, and other deeds its branches, leaves, flowers, and fruit.
rows.anchor: tasdîk-i kalbî onun tahte’l-arz kökü, ikrâr-ı lisân sâkı, a‘mâl-i sâire dalları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As losing branches or fruit does not by itself prove a tree dead, missing deeds do not make faith and deeds identical; lack of a trunk without excuse, however, suggests faith has not taken hold.
rows.anchor: yerle beraber kesilmiş olan ağaçların ‘ale’l-ekser kurudukları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A seed or root not yet sprouting in winter cannot be judged dead; likewise, inward assent during an excusable period need not be treated as dead faith.
rows.anchor: henüz topraktan filiz vermeyen tohumun veya kökün kuruduğuna hükmolunamayacağı gibi, mazeret zamanında tasdîk-i kalbî de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith has an essential core, then ordered degrees of branches and fruits; these latter belong to faith's perfection rather than its indispensable core.
rows.anchor: bir rükn-i aslîsi, bir rükn-i tâlîsi

rows.speaker: Peygamber
rows.claim: A Prophetic hadith calls faith more than seventy branches and names removing harm from the road as the least branch; Elmalılı takes this as a description of faith's perfection.
rows.anchor: İman yetmiş küsür şubedir. Bunların ednâsı yoldan eziyeti ref‘etmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling deeds branches signals they are not essential faith: their opposite entails sinfulness, not unbelief; the verse separately names belief, prayer, and spending.
rows.anchor: bu şu‘abât ve fürû‘, hilâfı küfür olan asl-ı îmân değil, hilâfı fısk olan kemâl-i îmândır ve bunun için bu âyette de “yü’minûn”, “ikāme-i salât” ve “infak” imandan ayrıca zikrolunmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says earlier statements by some Salaf and hadith scholars that label such branches faith should be understood as referring to faith's perfection.
rows.anchor: Bâlâda zikrolunan bazı selef ve muhaddisîn kavillerini de böyle anlamak lâzım gelir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı identifies the two essential acts of faith as inward assent and verbal profession, with profession waivable under legitimate necessity, and says this is Abu Hanifa's and most jurists' interpretation.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe hazretlerinin ve ‘âmme-i fukahânın da tefsir ve telakkīsidir.

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa defines faith as verbal profession plus assent in the heart; profession alone cannot suffice, or hypocrites would all count as believers.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe hazretlerinin ve ‘âmme-i fukahânın da tefsir ve telakkīsidir.

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa also rejects knowledge alone as faith, since that would make all People of the Book believers despite their recognizing the Prophet.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe hazretlerinin ve ‘âmme-i fukahânın da tefsir ve telakkīsidir.

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa distinguishes deeds from faith: one says a poor person owes no zakat, but does not say that the poor person lacks faith.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe hazretlerinin ve ‘âmme-i fukahânın da tefsir ve telakkīsidir.

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
rows.claim: In al-ʿĀlim wa-l-Mutaʿallim, Abu Hanifa says faith is called assent, recognition, profession, and Islam, and describes three combinations of heart and tongue.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe hazretlerinin ve ‘âmme-i fukahânın da tefsir ve telakkīsidir.

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
rows.claim: One who affirms God inwardly and verbally is a believer before both God and people.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe hazretlerinin ve ‘âmme-i fukahânın da tefsir ve telakkīsidir.

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
rows.claim: The person who professes with the tongue but inwardly denies is an unbeliever before God yet treated as a believer by people, who cannot inspect the heart.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe hazretlerinin ve ‘âmme-i fukahânın da tefsir ve telakkīsidir.

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
rows.claim: A person compelled to conceal inward faith is deemed an unbeliever by those unaware of the concealment but remains a believer before God.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe hazretlerinin ve ‘âmme-i fukahânın da tefsir ve telakkīsidir.

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa explains assent, knowledge, certainty, profession, and Islam as different names with one meaning: affirming and surrendering to God as Lord in heart and tongue.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe hazretlerinin ve ‘âmme-i fukahânın da tefsir ve telakkīsidir.

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa says the believer loves God above all else and would choose burning over falsely attributing a lie to God.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe hazretlerinin ve ‘âmme-i fukahânın da tefsir ve telakkīsidir.

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
rows.claim: The Fiqh al-Akbar teaching quoted here says believers are equal in faith and monotheism but differ in deeds, and that Islam is submission to divine commands.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe hazretlerinin ve ‘âmme-i fukahânın da tefsir ve telakkīsidir.

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
rows.claim: Lexically iman and Islam differ, but in religious usage neither exists without the other; they are a thing's inner and outer, while religion includes both and the whole Sharia.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe hazretlerinin ve ‘âmme-i fukahânın da tefsir ve telakkīsidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although iman is formally a verbal noun and thus an act, common and religious usage also makes it a noun denoting the settled condition initiated by that act.
rows.anchor: esasen masdar ve binâen‘aleyh bir fiil olmakla beraber örfen ve şer‘an isim olarak dahi kullanılır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam is not faith alone but the combination of faith and deeds; abandoning practical observance while expecting the religion's full benefit is dangerous.
rows.anchor: Tatbîkāt-ı ameliyeyi atıp da dinin feyz-i küllîsini beklemek tehlikelidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believing that a deed is obligatory differs from doing it: Muslims act because they believe, rather than becoming believers because they act.
rows.anchor: Müslüman amel ettiği için mü’min olacak değil, iman ettiği için amel edecektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone is not an unbeliever for omitting a deed unless the omission is solely from indifference or contempt for it.
rows.anchor: amelini sırf mübâlâtsızlıktan ve istihfaftan dolayı terk etmiş değil ise kâfir olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True Muslim faith begins in the heart, spreads through outward life, and yields good works for the world; it is not a destructive or devilish thought imprisoned inwardly.
rows.anchor: sonra kâinata mehâsin-i ameliye saçacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under severe enemy compulsion, one may conceal faith, but Elmalılı prefers risking one's life to free faith from concealment; he nevertheless allows either choice.
rows.anchor: O zaman da fedâ-yı nefs ederek imanını hapisden kurtarması, imanını hapsederek nefsini kurtarmasından müreccahtır. Ve ma‘amâfîh ikisi beyninde muhtârdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iqāmat al-salāt means more than merely praying: at least it means performing prayer correctly with measured movements and humility, and even leading it well.
rows.anchor: lâekal doğru dürüst yani ta‘dîl-i erkân ve huşû‘u hudû‘ile güzelce kılmak ve hatta kıldırmak mânalarını ifade eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because correct prayer matters, measured performance of its pillars is obligatory; striving to command right, forbid wrong, and complete the requirements of prayer is also an Islamic duty.
rows.anchor: olduğu gibi bilhassa namaz için emr bi’l-ma‘rûf ve nehy ‘ani’l-münker ve levâzım-ı salâtın istikmâli için sarf-ı mesâ‘î dahi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer education by parents, mutual reminders among believers, and rulers' removal of obstacles and encouragement—including care for Friday and congregational prayer—are among these duties.
rows.anchor: Ebeveynin evlâdına namaz terbiyesi, ihvân-ı dînin yekdiğerine tavsiye ve tezkîri, ulü’l-emrin izâle-i mevâni‘ve istikmâl-i esbâb ile tergīb ve teşvîki, cuma ve cemaate ihtimam ve ikdâmı da bu cümledendir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iqāma derives from setting upright, correcting, promoting, maintaining, or attending to something; applied to prayer, it evokes a shared sense of these meanings.
rows.anchor: “İkāme”, “kıyam” veya “kıvam”dan if‘âl olarak lügatta kaldırıp dikmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two-word expression iqāmat al-salāt was chosen over a single word meaning 'they pray' because it conveys more than the bare act of praying.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh “namaz kılarlar” demekle “ikāme-i salât ederler” demek arasında ne büyük fark vardır.

rows.speaker: Peygamber
rows.claim: A Prophetic hadith calls prayer the pillar of religion; Elmalılı uses its image of religion as a building and prayer as its pillar, with faith as its foundation.
rows.anchor: Bu hadiste din yüksek bir binâya teşbih ediliyor ve namaz aynı o

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse pictures prayer as a great pillar raised by the congregation, implying that the religious building must be constructed, protected, and maintained, with further structures built upon it.
rows.anchor: Bu âyette de namaz cemaatle kaldırılabilecek büyük bir direğe teşbih ediliyor ve onun güzelce dikilmesi veya doğrultulması suretiyle o yüksek binâ-yı dînin inşâ ve muhafaza ve idâmesi lüzûmu iş‘âr olunuyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Elmalılı's extended metaphor, God is the architect, the Prophet the chief foreman, and the community the workers; faith is laid in hearts, individual prayer prepares the pillar, and congregational prayer raises it publicly.
rows.anchor: Temsîlen diyebiliriz ki bu binânın mimarı Allah, baş kalfası Peygamber, amelesi ümmettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The religious building is alive and requires ongoing work by later generations; congregational prayer is the pillar and foundation of Islamic social organization, while individual prayer prepares it.
rows.anchor: Bu selef tarafından bir kere yapılmış olmakla sonradan gelenler, yalnız bunun içinde oturup kalacak değillerdir. O bir bünye-i zî-hayât gibi her gün yapılıp işletilecek, her gün nümuvv u inkişâfına hizmet edilecektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Upright prayer lets faith flourish through the whole person, gives life's course regular direction, purifies outward and inward life, and strengthens heart and body through practice.
rows.anchor: Bununla zâhir u bâtın mümkin olduğu kadar tasfiye ve kalb u beden mümarese ile takviye edilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Comparing a person's behavior when prayerless and when regularly praying shows moral improvement; the verse says prayer restrains indecency and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: اِنَّ الصَّلٰوةَ تَنْهٰى عَنِ الْفَحْشَٓاءِ وَالْمُنْكَرِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With regular observance, even a formal prayer gives four benefits: purification, strength of heart, ordered time, and social rectitude; its greatest benefits cannot be counted.
rows.anchor: Namazını kılan kimsenin hayatta lâekal dört kazancı vardır: Birincisi taharet, ikincisi kuvvet-i kalb, üçüncüsü intizâm-ı evkāt, dördüncüsü salâh-ı ictimâ‘î, ki bu fâideler devam şartıyla en resmî bir namazda bile vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At minimum, prayer breaks pride, prepares a person for brotherhood, and trains service for God's sake; wearing clean, fine clothes and repeatedly prostrating counters arrogance.
rows.anchor: Lâkin en asgarî fâide-i ahlâkiyesi bilfiil kibri kırmak, uhuvvete hazırlanmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arrogant people resist prostration because it forces them to place their ornamented foreheads on the ground; prayer is difficult except for the humble.
rows.anchor: yere koymak mecburiyeti onların kibir damarlarına, sinirlerine pek fena dokunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clothing and bodies are divine gifts and will return to dust; the earth itself deserves respect, since human life springs from it by God's creation.
rows.anchor: Düşünmezler ki o süsler, o alınlar hep ‘atâyâ-yı ilâhiyedir. Ve zamanı gelince o yağlı alınlar toza toprağa karışacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People's labor is implicated in one's possessions and clothing; prostrating to their Creator and joining congregational prayer helps free one from pride and selfishness and live fraternally.
rows.anchor: birtakım ‘ibâdullahın da hakları ta‘alluk etmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer breaks arrogance while raising the soul's freedom above the honor of appearing before the mightiest rulers; it is the believer's Miʿrāj, a ladder to divine presence.
rows.anchor: Namaz o kibr u gurûru kırarken aynı zamanda insanın rûh-i hürriyetine öyle bir i‘tilâ verir ki bu i‘tilâ en haşmetli hükümdarların huzûrundaki şeref-i müsûlden çok yüksektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer takes a person through life's stages—preparing, thinking, asking, standing, bowing, prostrating, sitting, and ending with peace—while teaching the mysteries of existence and the afterlife.
rows.anchor: İnsanı bütün hayatın kademelerinden geçirterek, esrâr-ı vücûdu, dünya ve uhrâyı düşündürerek Cenâb-ı Allah’a mülâkāt ettirir ve büyük bir iman ve sevab ile yine âleme avdet ettirir.

rows.speaker: Peygamber
rows.claim: Elmalılı cites a hadith that prayer distinguishes Islam from unbelief; he gives no grading here.
rows.anchor: Yine bir hadiste beyan olunduğu üzere namaz, İslâm ile küfrün fârikıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı cannot enumerate prayer's limitless worldly and otherworldly benefits; here he focuses on how prayer begins moral and social life and supports a great social structure, built through individual then congregational prayer.
rows.anchor: Biz burada namazın dünyevî ve uhrevî, maddî ve manevî bütün fezâil ve fevâidini sayacak değiliz. Çünkü o nâmütenâhîdir, nâkābil-i ihsâdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase iqāmat al-salāt conveys this social meaning fully; simply translating it as 'they pray' misses the force of the verse's description and praise of the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: tâbiriyle iktifâ etmek doğru değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-salāt is referential: it denotes the familiar Islamic prayer, with its known form and prescribed qualities.
rows.anchor: Burada الصَّلٰوة’ın elif lâmı ahd içindir ki, keyfiyeti mâlum ve ma‘hud olan İslâm namazı demektir.

rows.speaker: Peygamber
rows.claim: The Prophet's instruction to pray as he was seen praying establishes the ritual's form; its conditions and qualities were learned from his practice, words, and tacit approvals and transmitted continuously in practice.
rows.anchor: hadîs-i şerîfi mûcebince Peygamber’den görüldüğü ve fiilen ve kavlen ve takrîren ahz edildiği sıfat ve keyfiyettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic salāt has two lexical sources: unqualified supplication, and the verbal noun of ṣallā from ṣalw, referring to movement of the two hip projections as in bowing and prostration.
rows.anchor: “Salât” kelimesinin lügat-ı Arab’da iki me’hazı vardır. Birisi ‘ale’l-ıtlâk dua mânasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this second lexical sense, Arabs used ṣallā for moving the two salwins; an example says a horse or mare strikes its two hip-bones with its tail.
rows.anchor: at ve kısrak kuyruğuyla iki salvını sağa sola çarptı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı compares this bodily bending to the Jewish gesture called takfīr, a reverential bow involving the head and rear, and explains the anatomical sense of kāfireteyn.
rows.anchor: Yahudîler birbirine selâm ve tâzim sırasında başını eğer ve kıçını oynatıp kasığına doğru bir yan bükerlermiş ve bu tarz-ı selâma Arapça’da kâfireteyni tahrik mânasına “tekfir” ıtlak ederlermiş.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In religious usage, salāt names a complete, regular worship made of inward, spoken, and bodily acts and pillars, as received from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: İşte lügaten -biri kalb ve lisan işi olan dua, diğeri de bir hareket-i bedeniye işi olan fi‘l-i mahsus- iki mânaya gelen “salât” kelimesi şer‘an Peygamberimiz’den görülegeldiği üzere kalbî, lisânî, bedenî ef‘âl ve erkân-ı mahsûsadan mürekkeb gayet muntazam bir ibâdet-i kâmilenin ismi olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer has at least twelve obligatory elements: six external conditions and six internal pillars; it also has duties, Sunna acts, recommended acts, etiquette, disliked and invalidating acts, and several categories of prayers.
rows.anchor: necasetten taharet, hadesten taharet, setr-i avret, vakit, niyet, istikbâl-i kıble nâmıyla altısı dışından başlayan şart; iftitah tekbîri, kıyam, kıraat, rükû, sücud, teşehhüd mikdârı ka‘de-i ahîre nâmıyla içinde yapılan altı da rükn olmak üzere lâekal on iki farzı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Congregation is obligatory for Friday prayer and obligatory or emphasized Sunna for other prayers; here salāt primarily means the obligatory prayers.
rows.anchor: Cemaat dahi cumada farz, diğerlerinde vâcib veya sünnet-i müekkededir. Ve burada salâttan asl-ı murâd farz olanlardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām of salāt may be pronounced light or emphatic; it is written with wāw when emphatic, and Warsh also reads it emphatically.
rows.anchor: “Salât” kelimesinin lâm’ı ince de okunur kalın da ve kalın okunmak itibariyle “vâv”la yazılır, Verş kırâatinde de tefhīm olunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing do not stop at faith and bodily worship; they spend, in God's path, little or much of the material and even immaterial provision allotted to them.
rows.anchor: kendilerine nasib ve kısmet ettiğimiz rızıktan, maddî ve hatta manevî şeylerden az çok harç ve infak eder, fî-sebîlillâh sarfiyatta da bulunurlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mimmā is formed by assimilation from min mā; mā most closely corresponds to Turkish nesne, whereas man denotes a rational being, formerly distinguished as nesne and kimesne.
rows.anchor: مِمَّا idğam ile مِنْ مَا’dır. مَا kelimesinin Türkçemizde en güzel mukabili “nesne”dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā can broadly mean a thing, but its primary sense is a nonrational thing or things; man is used for rational beings.
rows.anchor: mukaddema مَا “nesne”, مَنْ “kimesne” diye tefrik edilirdi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq is basically a noun meaning a share or allotment, and also a verbal noun meaning to allot or provide; razaqnā is the verb, so mā here denotes a provision.
rows.anchor: “Rızk”, esasen kelâm-ı Arab’da haz ve nasib mânasına isim olup, nasib etmek, merzuk etmek mânasına masdar dahi olur ki رَزَقْنَا onun fiilidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Ahl al-Sunna, the legal sense of provision matches the lexical one: what God conveys to a living being and enables it actually to benefit from.
rows.anchor: Ehl-i sünnete göre ma‘nâ-yı şer‘îsi de lügavîsinin aynıdır ki “Cenâb-ı Allah’ın zî-hayâta sevk ve intifâ‘nasib ettiği şey” diye târif olunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Provision includes property actually eaten, drunk, or otherwise used whether owned or not, and also children, spouses, effort, work, knowledge, and learning; its benefit may be worldly or otherworldly.
rows.anchor: milk olsun olmasın, yenilen, içilen ve sâir suretle isti‘mâlinden bilfiil intifâ‘edilen emvâle sâdık olduğu gibi evlâda, zevceye, sa‘y u amele, ilm u ma‘ârife dahi şâmil olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Actual benefit is essential: wealth, family, children, or knowledge not actually used is not provision; one thing can be provision for different people according to their different uses.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh dinî veya dünyevî bilfiil intifâ‘edilmeyen mal, milk, evlâd u ‘iyâl, ilm u marifet rızk değildirler. Bu suretle bir şey muhtelif vücûh-i intifâ‘a göre muhtelif kimselerin rızkı olabilir.
